item.title: College of Charleston to celebrate new Phillis Wheatley stamp
item.description: The College of Charleston’s Avery Research Center on Friday will debut a new U.S. Postal Service stamp inspired by Phillis Wheatley, a once-enslaved woman who became America’s first published African American female poet. The post College of Charleston to celebrate new Phillis Wheatley stamp appeared first on Charleston City Paper.

item.title: McMaster to deliver State of the State tonight
item.description: For the ninth and final time, S.C. Gov. Henry McMaster will lay out his priorities in the annual State of the State address tonight at the state capitol. The post McMaster to deliver State of the State tonight appeared first on Charleston City Paper.

item.title: 2nd weekend of freezing weather has snow possibility
item.description: MORNING HEADLINES | The forecast for this weekend is just about what it was last weekend – really cold weather with a possibility of snow. But this weekend, the chance for up to an inch or so of snow around the Lowcountry is a little better. item.title: Our View: Congress must act now on ICE
item.description: The pounding of American democracy by masked bullethead thugs from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is unconscionable and immoral, particularly after a violent January. The post Our View: Congress must act now on ICE appeared first on Charleston City Paper.

item.title: Democrats raise alarms over S.C. immigration bill
item.description: After the killing of a second Minnesota protester last weekend by federal immigration officers, two Charleston-area Democratic lawmakers and the party’s leading candidate for governor are raising alarms about a bill in the S.C. House that they say could put local law enforcement officers and residents at risk. The post Democrats raise alarms over S.C. immigration bill appeared first on Charleston City Paper.
